368299.title: Jiang et al.'s forbidden-subgraph multiplicity conjecture
368299.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda>0$ and $p\in\mathbb{N}^+$. For a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of signed graphs, let $M_{p,\mathcal{F}}(\lambda,N)$ be the maximum of $\operatorname{mult}(-\lambda,G)$ over all $p$-colorable signed graphs $G$ on at most $N$ vertices that contain no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subgraph and satisfy $\lambda_{p+1}(G)\geq-\lambda$, where $\lambda_{p+1}(G)$ is the $(p+1)$-st smallest eigenvalue of $G$. **Jiang et al.'s forbidden-subgraph conjecture.** For every $\lambda>0$ and $p\in\mathbb{N}^+$, there exists a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of signed graphs such that $\lambda_1(F)<-\lambda$ for every $F\in\mathcal{F}$ and

$$
M_{p,\mathcal{F}}(\lambda,N)\leq
\begin{cases}
N/k_p(\lambda)+o(N) & \text{if }k_p(\lambda)<\infty,\\
o(N) & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture is the forbidden-subgraph estimate underlying the proposed asymptotic formula for $N_{\alpha,\beta}(d)$. The supplied context does not report a resolution, so the general assertion remains open.

368617.title: The Weak Graph Complement Conjectures
368617.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $G^c$ for its complement, $\operatorname{mr}(G)$ for minimum rank, $\operatorname{mr}_+(G)$ for positive semidefinite minimum rank, $\nu(G)$ for the positive semidefinite Colin de Verdière parameter, $\operatorname{mr}_\nu(G)=\ord G-\nu(G)$, and $\ord G$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**Weak Graph Complement Conjectures.** There exist universal constants $b,b_+,b_\nu<2$ such that, for every graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{mr}(G)+\operatorname{mr}(G^c)\leq b\cdot\ord G+2,
$$

$$
\operatorname{mr}_+(G)+\operatorname{mr}_+(G^c)\leq b_+\cdot\ord G+2,
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{mr}_\nu(G)+\operatorname{mr}_\nu(G^c)\leq b_\nu\cdot\ord G+2.
$$

These are weaker asymptotic forms of the three graph-complement conjectures. The source later states that the strongest version is resolved with constants at most $1.708$, but does not provide a general exact optimal constant in the supplied material.

363106.title: The counting conjecture for forbidden-poset-free set systems
363106.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset, and let a set system on $[n]$ be a family of subsets of $[n]$. Such a family is $P$-free if it contains no injective poset homomorphism from $P$. Let $e(P)$ be the largest integer $\ell$ such that, for all $j$ and $n$, the union

$$
\bigcup_{i=1}^{\ell}\binom{[n]}{i+j}
$$

is $P$-free.

**Counting conjecture for forbidden posets.** For every poset $P$, the number of $P$-free set systems in $2^{[n]}$ is

$$
2^{(1+o(1))e(P)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the asymptotic extremal-size conjecture and is the counting analogue of the forbidden-poset problem. The source gives no resolution status for the conjecture in general; the paper proves the asserted asymptotic count for fixed tree posets, where $e(P)=k-1$ when the height is $k$.

Need sharp containers/entropy bound at exact e(P), not merely an extremal-size bound. e(P)=0 exposes multiplicative-notation issues only, not significant credit. 358335.title: Frankl–Kupavskii's incompatibility conjecture for higher intersection parameters
358335.literal_statement:
Let $\Pi_1$ and $\Pi_2$ be monotone properties of families of subsets of $[n]$, and let $w(\mathcal{F})=|\mathcal{F}|/2^n$. The properties are **incompatible** when

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\left(\max_{\mathcal{F}_1\subset\mathcal{P}(n)\text{ has }\Pi_1}w(\mathcal{F}_1)\right)\left(\max_{\mathcal{F}_2\subset\mathcal{P}(n)\text{ has }\Pi_2}w(\mathcal{F}_2)\right)
$$

$$
=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\left(\max_{\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{P}(n)\text{ has }\Pi_1,\Pi_2}w(\mathcal{F})\right).
$$

**Frankl–Kupavskii's incompatibility conjecture.** For every integer $s\geq 1$ there exists an integer $t_0(s)$ such that for all $t\geq t_0(s)$, the properties of being 3-wise $s$-intersecting and $t$-intersecting are incompatible. By the Harris–Kleitman inequality, the joint maximum is always at least the product of the separate maxima, so the conjecture asserts asymptotic equality for sufficiently large $t$ depending on $s$. The source states that this conjecture remains open for all other values of $s$.
358335.derivation_and_gap: Need joint density bound for all fixed s and all t above a threshold depending on s. Harris-Kleitman is a lower bound, so does not prove equality. s=1 source case cannot pay all s. Original body unread.
358335.literal_light_feasibility: Finite-set maxima can be encoded lightly, but liminf equivalence and exact limiting constants unpaid.

358850.title: Bounded additive group irregularity strength for graphs without small components
358850.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with no connected components of order less than $3$. A **$\Gamma$-irregular labeling** is a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of an abelian group $\Gamma$ such that the induced vertex weights are pairwise distinct; denote the group irregularity strength by the least group order guaranteeing such a labeling for every abelian group of that order. **Bounded additive group irregularity conjecture.** There exists a constant $K$ such that every such graph $G$ has a $\Gamma$-irregular labeling for every group $\Gamma$ satisfying

$$
|\Gamma|\geq n+K.
$$

The conjecture asserts a uniform additive bound on the group irregularity strength for graphs whose components all have order at least $3$, extending the preceding bounds for broad classes of disconnected graphs. Its resolution would determine whether the dependence on the graph order can always be reduced to $n+O(1)$ in this setting.

355265.title: Bednarska-Bzdęga–Hefetz–Łuczak conjecture for Waiter–Client subgraph counts
355265.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with $e(H)\ge 1$, and let $m(H)$ denote its maximum density over nonempty subgraphs, namely

$$
m(H)=\max\left\{\frac{e(H')}{v(H')}:H'\subseteq H,\ v(H')\ge 1\right\}.
$$

Consider the $b$-Waiter–Client game on the edges of $K_n$, where Waiter offers $b$ previously unchosen edges in each round and Client chooses one, which is added to the resulting graph. **Bednarska-Bzdęga–Hefetz–Łuczak's Waiter–Client conjecture.** For every graph $H$ with $e(H)\ge 1$, there exist $c,\gamma>0$ such that, for $n$ sufficiently large and $b\le c n^{1/m(H)}$, Waiter can ensure that the resulting graph contains at least

$$
\frac{\gamma n^{v(H)}}{b^{e(H)}}
$$

copies of $H$. This conjecture asserts the direction complementary to the already proved regime $b\gg n^{1/m(H)}$, and formalizes the claim that the game follows the probabilistic intuition of a random graph with the same density.
355265.derivation_and_gap: No full Waiter strategy ensuring the correct H-count simultaneously over bias through c*n^(1/m(H)). Single edge or forest cases would be parameter instances; random-graph expectation does not force an adversarial strategy. Original source body unread despite suggestive title, so no public-proof exclusion asserted.

382017.title: Asymptotic extremal conjecture for ordered 3-uniform tight paths
382017.literal_statement:
Let $f(n,k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex ordered 3-uniform hypergraph avoiding the ordered tight-path configuration with parameter $k$, and let $P^{(3)}_s$ be the ordered 3-uniform tight path on $s$ vertices. Define

$$
a=\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor,
$$

and, equivalently,

$$
b=\left\lfloor\frac{(s-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Asymptotic extremal conjecture for ordered 3-uniform tight paths.** The constructions described in the source are asymptotically optimal: 

$$
f(n,k)=\left(1-\frac{1}{a}+o(1)\right)\binom{n}{3}.
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\mathrm{ex}_<(n,P^{(3)}_s)=\left(1-\frac{1}{b}+o(1)\right)\binom{n}{3}.
$$

The preceding constructions give the corresponding lower bounds, so the conjecture concerns matching asymptotic upper bounds for all relevant parameters.

350111.literal_statement:
Let a **$[k,n,1]$-graph** be a $k$-partite graph with parts of size $n$ and maximum degree at most $1$, and let $f(k)$ be the smallest integer $n_0$ such that every $[k,n,1]$-graph has a factor of independent transversals whenever $n\ge n_0$. Here, a factor of independent transversals is a partition of the vertices into independent sets, each containing exactly one vertex from every part.

$$
\nf(k)=\begin{cases}k,&\text{if }k\text{ is even},\\ k+1,&\text{if }k\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}

350119.title: Average minimum-degree conjecture for transversal cycle-factors
350119.literal_statement:
Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices, and let the **$n$-blow-up** of $C_k$ have parts $V_1,\dots,V_k$, each of size $n$. For a spanning subgraph $G$, let $\delta(G[V_i,V_{i+1}])$ denote the minimum degree in the bipartite graph between consecutive parts, with indices taken modulo $k$. A **transversal $C_k$-factor** is a collection of $n$ vertex-disjoint copies of $C_k$, each using one vertex from every part.

**Average minimum-degree conjecture.** For every $k\geq3$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n_0=n_0(k,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $n\geq n_0$, if there are numbers $\delta_1,\dots,\delta_k\geq n/2$ satisfying

$$
\delta(G[V_i,V_{i+1}])\geq\delta_i\quad\text{for every }i\in[k]
$$

and

$$
\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i\in[k]}\delta_i\geq\left(1+\frac{1}{k}+\varepsilon\right)\frac{n}{2},
$$

then $G$ has a transversal $C_k$-factor.

This conjecture strengthens the paper's asymptotic theorem by replacing a uniform degree condition with an average condition across the consecutive pairs. The preceding example shows that the corresponding threshold is close to best possible.
350119.derivation_and_gap: Separate perfect matchings on consecutive pairs can compose to nontrivial permutations with cycles winding multiple times through parts. Need a coordinated system whose composition is identity under the exact average degree threshold. A uniform min-degree theorem cannot simply use the average; original body unread.

348731.title: Generalized unbounded improvement conjecture for $(k,\ell)$-sum-free sets
348731.literal_statement:
Let $k<\ell$ be positive integers. For a set $A$ of $N$ positive integers, let $\mathscr{M}_{(k,\ell)}(A)$ be the size of its largest $(k,\ell)$-sum-free subset, where a set is **$(k,\ell)$-sum-free** if, for every $k+\ell$ elements $x_1,\dots,x_k,y_1,\dots,y_\ell$, one has

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k}x_i\ne\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}y_j.
$$

Define

$$
\mathscr{M}_{(k,\ell)}(N)=\inf_{A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{>0},\ |A|=N}\mathscr{M}_{(k,\ell)}(A).
$$

A **generalized $(k,\ell)$-sum-free conjecture.** There is a function $\omega(N)\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$ such that for every set $A$ of $N$ positive integers, there exists a maximal $(k,\ell)$-sum-free set $\Omega(k,\ell)\subseteq\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ for which

$$
\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\sum_{n\in A}\left(\mathbbm{1}_{\Omega(k,\ell)}-\frac{1}{k+\ell}\right)(nx)=\omega(N).
$$

The known asymptotic formula $\mathscr{M}_{(k,\ell)}(N)=N/(k+\ell)+o(N)$ leaves open whether every pair $(k,\ell)$ admits an unbounded improvement over the probabilistic baseline $N/(k+\ell)$.

Need source precise maximal-torus-set convention, a lower discrepancy diverging with N and all k<ell. Original body unread; equality-to-omega wording alone is not a result.

331182.title: The $r$-adjacent strong chromatic index conjecture
331182.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, two distinct vertices are **$r$-adjacent** if their distance is at most $r$. Let $\chi'_{a,r}(G)$ denote the least number of colours in a proper edge colouring of $G$ such that the sets of colours incident with any two $r$-adjacent vertices are distinct. Write $\Delta(G)$ and $\delta(G)$ for the maximum and minimum degrees of $G$, respectively.

**The $r$-adjacent strong chromatic index conjecture.** For each positive integer $r$ there exist constants $\delta_0$ and $C$ such that

$$
\chi'_{a,r}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+C
$$

328512.title: Induced forbidden subposet density conjecture
328512.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a poset. Write $B_n$ for the Boolean poset of all subsets of $[n]$, and let $La^*(n,P)$ be the maximum size of an induced $P$-free subposet of $B_n$. Define

$$
e^*(P)=\text{the largest integer }k\text{ such that, for every }j\text{ and }n,\ \bigcup_{i=1}^k\binom{[n]}{j+i}\text{ is induced }P\text{-free}.
$$

**Induced forbidden subposet density conjecture.** The limit

$$
\pi^*(P)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{La^*(n,P)}{\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}
$$

exists and

$$
\pi^*(P)=e^*(P).
$$

This is the induced analogue of the ordinary forbidden subposet density conjecture. The source notes that only limited results were known: an asymptotic upper bound was established for every poset, and the induced analogue was proved for tree posets with an $o(1)$ error term, but the conjecture remains open in general.

323202.title: The component and fragment conjecture for bridge-addable graph classes
323202.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a set of graphs, let $R_n \in_u {\mathcal A}$ be uniformly distributed over its graphs on vertex set $[n]$, let $\kappa(R_n)$ denote the number of components of $R_n$, and let $\operatorname{frag}(R_n)$ denote the number of vertices outside a largest component. A graph class is **bridge-addable** if adding an edge between two distinct components of any graph in the class produces a graph still in the class. **The component and fragment conjecture.** If ${\mathcal A}$ is bridge-addable and $R_n \in_u {\mathcal A}$, then, asymptotically,

$$
\kappa(R_n) \leq_s 1+\operatorname{Po}\left(\frac12\right),
$$

and

$$
\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb E[\operatorname{frag}(R_n)] \leq 1.
$$

This conjecture seeks the forest-optimal asymptotic bounds for the number of components and the fragment under the weaker bridge-addable hypothesis. Part (a) was known with a weaker Poisson parameter, while the full claims were presented as open in the source.
323202.derivation_and_gap: Bridge-addability supplies legal merging edges, but expectation of fragment needs tail control weighted by fragment size. Component-count stochastic bound alone does not control a rare large fragment. Need both exact Poisson-half domination and expectation<=1 for arbitrary class. Original body unread.

381021.title: The level-count conjecture for forbidden subposets
381021.literal_statement:
Let $P$subseteq be a finite poset. Let $\operatorname{Mon}(\mathbb{Z})$ be the set of functions $f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}$ such that $f(n)=1$ and $f(-n)=0$ for all sufficiently large $n$, ordered pointwise. A **level** is a maximal family $L\subset\operatorname{Mon}(\mathbb{Z})$ on which $\sum_n f(n)-g(n)=0$ for every $f,g\in L$. Define $l(P)$ to be the maximum number of levels whose union does not contain $P$ as a subposet. **Level-count conjecture.** For every finite poset $P$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}(P,n)=l(P)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\bigl(1+O(1/n)\bigr).
$$

This conjecture proposes a common asymptotic explanation for several known forbidden-subposet results, including those for chains, brooms, butterflies, and loops on adjacent levels of the Boolean lattice. Its general validity is not established by the surrounding discussion.

Infinite level definition/degenerate l(P)=0 multiplicative form needs source fidelity; a wording correction earns zero. Original body unread.

335586.title: The asymptotic sharpness conjecture for Betti numbers of complexes with highly connected links
335586.literal_statement:
Let $k$ and $\ell$ be integers with $0\leq \ell<k$, and let $B_{n,k,\ell}$ be the bound defined in the paper. For a simplicial complex $X$ with

$$
\Delta_{n-1}^{(k-1)}\subset X\subset\Delta_{n-1}^{(k)},
$$

write $\lambda_{\ell,k-\ell-2}(X)$ for the relevant link-connectivity parameter and $\tilde{\beta}_{k-1}(X)$ for its reduced Betti number. **The asymptotic sharpness conjecture.** For any fixed $0\leq \ell<k$, there exists a constant $n_0(k,\ell)$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0(k,\ell)$ and $B_{n,k,\ell}$ is an integer, there exists a complex $\Delta_{n-1}^{(k-1)}\subset X\subset\Delta_{n-1}^{(k)}$ such that $\lambda_{\ell,k-\ell-2}(X)=0$ and

$$
\tilde{\beta}_{k-1}(X)=B_{n,k,\ell}.
$$

The preceding results show that $B_{n,k,\ell}$ is an upper bound under the corresponding link-connectivity condition and is asymptotically tight for fixed $k,\ell$ as $n\to\infty$; the conjecture asserts exact attainment for all sufficiently large $n$ for which the bound is integral.

329093.title: The asymptotic lower-bound conjecture for Nullstellensatz certificates of graph-coloring ideals
329093.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb K$ be a field, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be a graph. A **Nullstellensatz certificate** of the $k$-coloring ideal of $G$ is an identity certifying that $G$ is not $k$-colorable, and its degree is the degree of that certificate.

**Asymptotic certificate-degree conjecture.** For every field $\mathbb K$ and every positive integer $m$, there exists a constant $k_0$ with the following property: for each $k>k_0$ and every non-$k$-colorable graph $G$, every Nullstellensatz certificate of the $k$-coloring ideal of $G$ has degree at least $mk+1$.

The conjecture proposes that the lower bound on certificate degree grows by an arbitrarily prescribed multiple of the number of colors for sufficiently large $k$. It is motivated by computational evidence that the basic lower bound $N_{k,\mathbb K}(G)\geq k+1$ is not tight for large $k$.

375407.title: Alon's asymptotic subgraph-count conjecture
375407.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a fixed finite simple graph without isolated vertices. For a graph $G$, let $N(G,H)$ be the number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $H$, let

$$
N(m,H)=\max\{N(G,H):e(G)=m\},
$$

and define

$$
\gamma(H)=\frac{|V(H)|+D(H)}{2},\qquad D(H)=\max_{S\subseteq V(H)}\bigl(|S|-|N_H(S)|\bigr).
$$

**Alon's asymptotic subgraph-count conjecture.** There is a positive constant $b(H)$ such that

$$
\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{N(m,H)}{m^{\gamma(H)}}=b(H).
$$

Alon proved the order of growth $N(m,H)=\Theta_H(m^{\gamma(H)})$ for every fixed $H$, and determined the exact leading constant when $D(H)=0$. The conjecture asks for the existence of the asymptotic leading constant in general.
